# Community conduct

WISE's issue tracker and contribution spaces should be useful, respectful and safe for participants with different experience levels and backgrounds.

## Expected behavior

- Discuss ideas and evidence without attacking people.
- Give actionable feedback and accept that reviewers may ask for smaller changes or stronger tests.
- Respect privacy, authorization boundaries, attribution and third-party licenses.
- Keep discussion relevant and disclose conflicts of interest when they matter.
- Use inclusive language; assume questions can be asked in good faith.

Harassment, threats, hateful language, impersonation, doxxing, credential disclosure, spam and unauthorized attacks are not acceptable. Do not publish private messages or personal information without permission.

## Moderation and reporting

The repository owner and maintainers may edit/remove harmful content, close or lock discussions, or restrict participation. Responses should be proportionate to the behavior and context; mistakes may be addressed with clarification or a warning.

Report concerns through an existing private channel with [the repository owner](https://github.com/qwzx4893-stack). If none is available, request a private contact route without posting personal details or the sensitive report publicly. No dedicated moderation inbox or response-time commitment has been established.

Security findings follow the separate [security policy](../SECURITY.md). These guidelines apply to the repository's issues, pull requests and other project-managed discussion spaces; they do not create a software license or support guarantee.
